neighbours.label: a verb of something adorning, wrapping or marking a body or surface (decorated, wrapped, encircled, marked), at the verb and its object's determiner
fire: A string of pearls encircled her slender neck.
Gold leaf adorned the ceiling of the great hall.
Thick bandages swathed his injured arm.
Long silver hair framed her pale face.
Bright murals decorated the walls of the station.
A wreath of laurel crowned the victor's head.
Years of distrust marked the relationship between the two towns.
A faded scarf wrapped the old man's throat.
quiet: A string of pearls was sold at the market.
Gold leaf was shipped to the great hall.
Thick bandages arrived for his injured arm.
Long silver hair was cut in the salon.
Bright murals were painted last year by students.
A wreath of laurel was ordered for the ceremony.
Years of distrust ended after the two towns met.
A faded scarf was left on the bus.

notes: Card: 'investing his neck', 'decorated its churches', 'haloing his head', 'marked the transition'. Probe: decorated/wrapped/marked 0.5-0.8, covered 0.18, sold 0.02. Near misses keep the same subjects and objects with plain transactional or movement verbs.
